definition: A practised feel for a particular machine’s tendencies — where it drifts, what it over-does, which phrasings it obeys; the promptwright’s knowledge of the material.
etymology: From grain (Latin granum, ‘seed’; the direction of fibres in wood) + sense. After the carpenter’s first rule: work with the grain.
in_context: Grainsense is why her prompts transfer badly — they’re tuned to one model’s wood.
the_case: The thesis of the whole volume in a single word: this is a material craft, and the material has a grain.
seo_title: grainsense — knowing how one particular AI model behaves
seo_description: Why a prompt that works on one model fails on another. Grainsense is the practised feel for a machine’s tendencies — where it drifts, which phrasings it obeys.
